    Case study

    I turned loan-level auto-loan data into a model that answers what a credit committee asks: how big is the pool, where is delinquency, how are losses trending, and what happens to expected loss if credit quality worsens.

    The data

    • 500 loans with 58 fields each.
    • 6,000 monthly delinquency snapshots.
    • 12 months of collections, losses and prepayments.
    • 15 quarterly vintages, 2021-Q1 to 2024-Q3.

    What I found

    • 77% of loans (385 of 500) are current.
    • Stage 3 holds 7.22M of the 11.66M ECL (61.9%).
    • New vehicle purchase loans carry the largest ECL.
    • Collections of 224.31M against 114.32M scheduled, with a spike in May.

    How I checked it

    • I rebuilt ECL for all 500 loans in Excel. It matches Power BI to rounding.
    • At 5% stress, Excel gives 12.25M, the same as the dashboard.
    • I reconciled the monthly balance roll-forward and loss figures.

    What it does not cover

    • It is project data, not live institutional data.
    • The brief asked for 8+ pages, 80+ measures and row-level security. I built six pages and no role security.
    • The data has no tranche-level fee fields, so I did not invent a full waterfall.
